Keywords: Shvarno marriage and Black Ruthenian claims
RagShortTexts: Shvarno married a daughter of Mindaugas.
Marriage ties coexist with competing claims in Black Ruthenia.

Variants.Content: Shvarno’s marriage to Mindaugas’ daughter gives the families kinship and channels for mediation. Black Ruthenian towns and offices remain contested. Hospitality, promises and local recognition make the relationship effective; kinship alone does not command every garrison.
Marriage envoys carry gifts, not automatic garrison rights. Escorts establish residence and provisioning responsibilities before a friendly visit becomes a dispute over a strongpoint.
Marriage eases disputes while creating expectations. Black Ruthenian settlements need identifiable consent; kin titles cannot replace agreement by towns and holders of power.
Envoys bring trade but consume lodging and food. Households judge marriage by reduced raids and demands and need collectors who acknowledge prior payments.
